newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha higher, LSWR rumoured sold to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha higher, LSWR rumoured sold to U.S..

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices bounced higher on Tuesday after having taken support from firmer European naphtha as well as stronger overnight crude oil markets, traders said.
First-half July open-spec naphtha was assessed at $207.00/209.00 per tonne, compared to late Monday's levels of $206.00/206.50.

Near-term spreads remained in contango, with the second-half June contract quoted about $1.00 lower than second-half July. The one-month spread from first-half July was assessed in backwardation at plus 50 cents.
In term naphtha talks for Saudi Arabian cargoes, potential buyers in Japan and South Korea have yet to hear from Saudi Aramco after the first round of bidding closed on April 4.
Traders expected the supplier to notify them of the place and date of face-to-face negotiations later this week.
In low-sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) trade, one million barrels of April-lifting Indonesian cargoes were rumoured to have been sold to the United States.
Even if the cargoes have actually been placed, sentiment for April-lifting cargoes is expected to remain on the bearish side amid depressed regional demand, traders said.
